To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the selectivity of binding of macrocycle ionophores to alkali metal cation is enhanced by the presence of the bulky RTIL anion.
the selectivity of cyclodextrin- and calixareneresponsive macrocycles in ionic liquids is different from the selectivity in solventfree conditions and in water-methanol mixtures.

the binding selectivities of cyclodextrins and related calixarenes for alkali metal cation guests in room-temperature ILs are substantially different than those measured in aqueous solution or under solvent-free conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the design of selective macrocycle ionophores for RTILs, which may be of interest in the field of ion sensors and ion-selective electrodes.
the development of a new experimental approach to determine binding selectivities of macrocycles and the rationalization of the selectivity trends in RTILs in terms of the solvation effects.
the understanding of the binding properties and selectivities of macrocyclic hosts in RTILs.

the selectivity of ionophores in ionic liquid media depends on the nature of the ionophore, the nature of the ionic liquid, and the cation to be recognized.
the binding selectivity of the macrocyclic ionophores in the ionic liquid solutions is a combination of the intrinsic binding selectivities and solvation effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the binding of macrocycle ionophores in RTILs is dominated by the steric effects of the RTIL counterions, whereas in the absence of solvents, the ionophoric properties of these receptors are governed by the electrostatics of the cations.
the binding selectivity of macrocycles in the presence of the ionic liquid can be rationalized in terms of the steric interactions between the ionophore and the ionic liquid counterion.
the binding selectivity of ionophores can be substantially altered by solvation in the RTIL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
solvation can play a crucial role in determining the selectivities of macrocycle ionophores in RTILs, and thus the design of new RTIL-based ion sensors.
RTILs can be used to modulate the selectivity of binding of macrocyclic hosts toward metal cations, which may be useful for the design of new ionophores.

the ionophoric behavior of the studied macrocycles is significantly affected by solvation effects, and that the binding selectivity in RTILs can be tuned by changing the nature of the side substituents on the macrocyclic ring.
